SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D REGISTRY
No. L. O. 4182
File No. 22.5.29.
POLITICAL BRANCH
(FOREIGN SECTION)
DATE 29.5.29

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
/D.C.I.

C.I.D. 3585
A. 702
A. 8263.

With reference to the attached memo from the Atg. D.C.P.
there are only three files on record referring to persons of
similar names. Two of these refer to Ralph S. Boyd who was
convicted in the American Court in 1922 and who left for the
States in 1926, and the other concerns C.F. Carpenter a British
subject who obtained goods on credit from several local firms
and who absconded in June 1926.

These files are attached and were not forwarded in the
first instance as they do not appear to refer to the same person
as Mr. Boyd Carpenter of whom there is nothing on record.

J.R.
22/5/29.

J.H. Rew
mk

J. Robertson
D. I.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记室
编号 L. O. 4182
档案号 22.5.29.
政治部
（外籍股）
日期 1929年5月29日

（刑事侦缉处）办公笔记
/副巡捕总监

刑事侦缉处 3585
A. 702
A. 8263.

关于附呈的代理副巡捕总监备忘录，记录在案且姓名相似的人员档案仅有三份。其中两份涉及拉尔夫·S·博伊德（Ralph S. Boyd），此人于1922年在美国法院被判有罪，并于1926年前往美国；另一份涉及英国臣民 C.F.卡彭特（C.F. Carpenter），此人从本地多家商行赊购货物，并于1926年6月潜逃。

上述档案随函附上，起初未予转送，是因为它们似乎并非指代博伊德·卡彭特（Boyd Carpenter）先生，而关于此人在档案中并无任何记录。

J.R.
1929年5月22日

J.H. Rew
mk

J. Robertson
督察长

pages.en:
8/201

I seem to remember a man
of this name who made
himself generally obnoxious
at a Race meeting some
years ago and was removed from
the Race Club Compound by either
Dick or Burnside. What I
remember of the man was that
he claimed to have a vast
experience of racing in Australia
& spoke with an Australian
accent & had no status & I think
poorly marked and was in some
way connected with pearls or a
deal in pearls. I seem also to remember hearing
later that he got into trouble up in
the North Tientsin or Peking later
and that they wrote down to us for
information.

[Signature]
For Secy: [Signature]
my per [Signature]
pages.zh:
8/201

我似乎记得有这么一个人，
几年前在一次赛马会上
表现得极其令人讨厌，
后来被迪克（Dick）或伯恩赛德（Burnside）
逐出了赛马会会所大院。
我对这人的印象是，他声称自己在澳大利亚
拥有丰富的赛马经验，
说话带有澳大利亚口音，
没有任何社会地位，而且我觉得他
相貌平平，并以某种方式与珍珠
或珍珠交易有关。我似乎还依稀记得后来听说
他在北方的天津或北京惹上了麻烦，
那边曾写信向我们查询
有关他的信息。

[签名]
代秘书：[签名]
经我手 [签名]

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 182
Date 29. 5. 29

May 21, 29

My dear Jamieson,

Mr. Boyd Carpenter

With reference to your note of April 20,
no trace can be found of a person bearing the name
of Boyd Carpenter having ever visited Shanghai.

Should any information come to light
regarding this individual, it will be forwarded to
you without delay.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd) R.M.J. Martin.

E. G. Jamieson Esq., C.B.E.,
H.B.M. Consulate General.

JMJ
Recd.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 182
BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
Date. 23. 4. 29.
SHANGHAI.
P.O.Box 259.
20th April, 1929.

Confidential.

My dear Martin,
We have been asked for information
concerning a certain Mr. Boyd Carpenter.
He is understood to be a British subject and
to have been in China at some time or other,
but I have no further particulars, although
the name seems familiar to me. Would you be
so good as to ask whether any of your people
know anything about the man?
Yours sincerely,
E. G. Jamieson

Captain R. M. J. Martin,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

机密

亲爱的马丁：

我方被要求提供关于某位博伊德·卡彭特先生的信息。
据悉他为英国臣民，并曾在某个时期到过中国，
但我没有更多详情，尽管这个名字对我来说似乎有些耳熟。能否请您
询问一下贵处人员是否了解此人的情况？
此致
敬礼，
E. G. 杰米森
